This report re-analyses the simulated pricing A/B test in R, independently of the
Python toolkit, as a cross-check. Generate the data first:

```bash
python scripts/pricing_experiment.py   # writes reports/data/pricing_experiment.csv
quarto render reports/pricing_experiment.qmd
```

```{r}
#| label: load
df <- read.csv("data/pricing_experiment.csv")
df$treated <- df$arm == "treatment"
table(df$arm)
```

## Raw comparison

Revenue per shipper is heavy-tailed, so the raw test is noisy.

```{r}
#| label: raw
raw <- t.test(revenue ~ treated, data = df)  # Welch by default
raw
```

## CUPED with pre-period revenue

```{r}
#| label: cuped
theta <- cov(df$revenue, df$pre_revenue) / var(df$pre_revenue)
df$revenue_cuped <- df$revenue - theta * (df$pre_revenue - mean(df$pre_revenue))
cat(sprintf("theta = %.3f, variance reduction = %.0f%%\n",
            theta, 100 * (1 - var(df$revenue_cuped) / var(df$revenue))))
adj <- t.test(revenue_cuped ~ treated, data = df)
adj
lift <- diff(rev(adj$estimate)) / adj$estimate[["mean in group FALSE"]]
cat(sprintf("relative lift (treatment vs control): %+.1f%%\n", 100 * lift))
```

The same estimate as a regression with the covariate, which also gives a
heteroskedasticity-robust standard error:

```{r}
#| label: ancova
fit <- lm(revenue ~ treated + pre_revenue, data = df)
X <- model.matrix(fit)
e <- residuals(fit)
bread <- solve(crossprod(X))
hc1 <- bread %*% crossprod(X * e) %*% bread * nrow(X) / (nrow(X) - ncol(X))
est <- coef(fit)[["treatedTRUE"]]
se <- sqrt(hc1["treatedTRUE", "treatedTRUE"])
cat(sprintf("treatment effect %.0f USD/shipper, 95%% CI [%.0f, %.0f]\n",
            est, est - 1.96 * se, est + 1.96 * se))
```

## Who reacts to price

```{r}
#| label: segments
seg <- aggregate(revenue ~ segment + arm, data = df, FUN = mean)
wide <- reshape(seg, idvar = "segment", timevar = "arm", direction = "wide")
wide$lift_pct <- round(100 * (wide$revenue.treatment / wide$revenue.control - 1), 1)
wide[order(wide$lift_pct), c("segment", "lift_pct")]
```

## Recommendation

A blanket 5% increase lowers revenue per shipper, driven by e-commerce and regional
forwarders. Pharma shippers are the exception, which matches the price-response
curves in `cargokit.optimize.pricing`: price by segment, not across the board.
